courseDetails.title: Principles of Public Relations
courseDetails.description: A 100-level Mass Communication course covering the foundations, objectives, ethics, theories, planning, media relations, internal communication, public-sector and non-profit PR, and evaluation of public relations activities.

questions.question: Which definition best reflects Grunig and Hunt's view of public relations?
options: The purchase of media space to increase sales
The one-way distribution of favourable publicity
The management of communication between an organisation and its publics
The design of products for selected markets
questions.explanation: Grunig and Hunt defined PR as managing communication between an organisation and its publics, shifting attention towards strategic relationship management.

questions.question: What major idea did the PRSA's 2012 definition emphasise?
options: Building mutually beneficial relationships between organisations and their publics
Replacing research with intuition
Using only paid advertising channels
Limiting communication to senior management
questions.explanation: The PRSA definition presents PR as a strategic communication process that builds relationships benefiting both the organisation and its publics.

questions.question: Which early PR pioneer issued the Declaration of Principles in 1906?
options: Edward Bernays
James Grunig
Scott Cutlip
Ivy Lee
questions.explanation: Ivy Lee's Declaration of Principles promoted openness, accuracy, and honest dealings with the press.

questions.question: What was Edward Bernays especially known for contributing to public relations?
options: Establishing the first Nigerian PR institute
Applying psychological and social-science ideas to shape public opinion
Creating the Barcelona Principles
Inventing social media monitoring
questions.explanation: Bernays applied insights from psychology and social science to persuasion and public-opinion management.

questions.question: Which organisation was established in 1900 and is commonly identified as the first public relations agency?
options: The Publicity Bureau
The Public Relations Society of America
The International Public Relations Association
The National Broadcasting Commission
questions.explanation: The Publicity Bureau, founded in 1900, is commonly described in the course as the first modern PR agency.

questions.question: What development most clearly marked the professionalisation of PR in the mid-twentieth century?
options: The complete abandonment of print media
The replacement of PR by advertising
The formation of professional bodies and university PR programmes
The end of organisational communication
questions.explanation: Bodies such as PRSA and IPRA, together with formal PR education, helped establish PR as a recognised profession.

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes early PR from contemporary strategic PR?
options: Early PR relied on social media, while modern PR avoids technology
Early PR was mainly one-way publicity, while contemporary PR emphasises relationships and strategy
Early PR focused on employees, while modern PR ignores internal publics
Early PR measured outcomes, while modern PR rejects evaluation
questions.explanation: Early practice concentrated on getting information out; modern PR is planned, interactive, ethical, and relationship-focused.

questions.question: How did the digital revolution change public relations most directly?
options: It removed the need for reputation management
It made journalists irrelevant in every situation
It restricted PR to printed publications
It enabled real-time, two-way engagement with publics
questions.explanation: Digital platforms allow organisations and publics to interact directly and continuously, creating a 24-hour communication environment.

questions.question: Why is public relations described as a continuous process?
options: Every campaign must run permanently without review
PR can only be practised by full-time journalists
Relationships and public perceptions require ongoing management
An organisation must publish a press release every day
questions.explanation: PR is not a single event; organisations must repeatedly listen, communicate, evaluate, and maintain stakeholder relationships.

questions.question: Which statement best captures the strategic nature of modern PR?
options: PR activities are deliberately planned to support organisational goals
PR messages are released randomly whenever publicity is available
PR is limited to responding after crises occur
PR decisions are made without research or evaluation
questions.explanation: Strategic PR uses research, objectives, planning, execution, and evaluation to contribute to wider organisational goals.

questions.question: Which PR objective focuses on helping an organisation become recognisable to its target publics?
options: Reducing stakeholder contact
Building brand awareness
Eliminating media coverage
Restricting internal communication
questions.explanation: Brand awareness helps an organisation stand out and become familiar to the people it seeks to reach.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of media relations in PR?
options: To buy every available advertising space
To prevent journalists from asking questions
To replace all direct stakeholder communication
To build productive relationships with journalists and secure credible coverage
questions.explanation: Media relations involves working with journalists, bloggers, and other intermediaries to support accurate and favourable coverage.

questions.question: A company identifies possible product-safety complaints before they occur and prepares response messages. Which PR function is illustrated?
options: Crisis anticipation and planning
Employee recruitment
Market price setting
Routine product distribution
questions.explanation: Crisis management begins before a crisis through risk identification, preparation, designated responsibilities, and response planning.

questions.question: Why is transparent communication especially important during a crisis?
options: It guarantees that the organisation will receive no criticism
It allows the organisation to hide uncertain facts
It helps maintain credibility by providing timely and honest information
It replaces the need to listen to stakeholders
questions.explanation: Honest, timely updates reduce rumours and show that the organisation is taking responsibility.

questions.question: Which activity best demonstrates community relations?
options: Purchasing television airtime for a product advert
Partnering with local groups to support a community health programme
Changing the company's wholesale price
Closing all channels for public feedback
questions.explanation: Community relations builds goodwill through participation, sponsorship, volunteering, partnerships, and social responsibility.

questions.question: How does corporate social responsibility support public relations?
options: It guarantees positive coverage regardless of conduct
It allows a company to avoid accountability
It focuses only on increasing short-term sales
It demonstrates an organisation's commitment to social and environmental responsibilities
questions.explanation: Credible CSR initiatives show that an organisation contributes to broader social goals and can strengthen stakeholder trust.

questions.question: What most directly strengthens organisational credibility?
options: Accurate information, ethical conduct, and consistent messaging
Frequent exaggeration and secrecy
Different claims on every platform
Avoiding corrections when mistakes occur
questions.explanation: Credibility grows when communication is truthful, actions are ethical, and messages remain coherent across channels.

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares PR and advertising?
options: PR always controls final media wording more than advertising
Advertising is always two-way, while PR is never interactive
PR often relies on earned credibility, while advertising pays for controlled message placement
PR and advertising have identical objectives and methods
questions.explanation: Advertising purchases space or time and offers high message control; PR often gains third-party coverage with less control but greater perceived credibility.

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes PR from marketing?
options: PR is only concerned with sales, while marketing manages government relations
Marketing uses research, while PR never does
PR uses communication, while marketing does not
PR manages relationships with broad stakeholder groups, while marketing concentrates mainly on customers and exchange
questions.explanation: PR addresses employees, media, investors, communities, regulators, and customers; marketing primarily aims to create and satisfy customer demand.

questions.question: How can PR support a marketing campaign without becoming advertising?
options: By purchasing all media placements directly
By generating credible media coverage and stakeholder interest around the product
By setting the retail price of the product
By replacing product development decisions
questions.explanation: PR can amplify marketing through earned media, influencer relations, events, and reputation-building rather than paid placement alone.

questions.question: Which principle requires PR practitioners to provide information that is accurate and not misleading?
options: Honesty and transparency
Message saturation
Selective disclosure
Competitive secrecy
questions.explanation: Honesty and transparency are central to credibility and require accurate, accessible, and timely communication.

questions.question: What does serving the public interest require from a PR practitioner?
options: Defending the organisation regardless of harm
Ignoring all stakeholder concerns
Considering the wider social effects of organisational decisions
Publishing only messages that increase profit
questions.explanation: Ethical PR balances organisational interests with the legitimate needs, safety, and welfare of the public.

questions.question: Which action best demonstrates integrity in public relations?
options: Deleting criticism without investigation
Admitting and correcting a material error in an official statement
Inventing statistics to strengthen a campaign
Concealing a known public-safety risk
questions.explanation: Integrity requires consistency between ethical principles, communication, and conduct, including correcting mistakes.

questions.question: Why is two-way communication valuable in PR?
options: It gives the organisation complete control over public opinion
It removes the need for planning
It prevents publics from expressing disagreement
It enables dialogue, feedback, and mutual understanding
questions.explanation: Two-way communication allows organisations to listen and adapt instead of merely transmitting messages.

questions.question: A campaign uses images and language that respect different ethnic, religious, and social groups. Which principle is being applied?
options: Press agentry
Message secrecy
Diversity and inclusivity
Market exclusion
questions.explanation: Inclusive PR recognises differences among publics and avoids stereotypes, exclusion, or culturally insensitive communication.

questions.question: When does PR become strategic according to the approach discussed in the course?
options: When it identifies publics that can help or hinder organisational goals
When it produces the largest number of press releases
When it operates separately from management
When it focuses only on short-term publicity
questions.explanation: Strategic PR identifies consequential publics and manages communication in ways that support long-term organisational goals.

questions.question: What is stakeholder mapping?
options: Listing only the organisation's paying customers
Ranking media outlets by advertising price
Drawing the physical location of company offices
Identifying groups that affect or are affected by an organisation
questions.explanation: Stakeholder mapping identifies relevant groups such as employees, customers, investors, regulators, communities, and media.

questions.question: Why are stakeholders prioritised in strategic PR?
options: Every stakeholder must receive an identical message
Their influence and potential impact on organisational goals differ
Only hostile stakeholders matter
Prioritisation eliminates the need for engagement
questions.explanation: Prioritisation helps allocate attention and resources according to stakeholder power, interest, urgency, and relevance.

questions.question: Which research activity involves monitoring social, political, economic, and technological developments?
options: Environmental scanning
Copy editing
Media buying
Product packaging
questions.explanation: Environmental scanning tracks external trends, risks, and opportunities that may affect the organisation.

questions.question: What is proactive issues management designed to achieve?
options: Create publicity after every crisis
Avoid all communication with critics
Identify and address emerging concerns before they become crises
Delay decisions until public pressure becomes severe
questions.explanation: Issues management uses scanning, risk assessment, scenario planning, and stakeholder engagement to prevent escalation.

questions.question: In the RACE framework, what does the first letter represent?
options: Reach
Reputation
Response
Research
questions.explanation: In the course's PR planning framework, RACE stands for Research, Action, Communication, and Evaluation.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a situation analysis in a PR plan?
options: To select slogans before gathering evidence
To assess internal and external factors affecting the communication problem
To calculate only advertising costs
To write the final evaluation report first
questions.explanation: Situation analysis establishes the starting point and can use tools such as SWOT and PESTLE.

questions.question: Which item is an internal factor in a SWOT analysis?
options: A new government regulation
A competitor entering the market
A weakness in the organisation's communication capacity
A change in public attitudes
questions.explanation: Strengths and weaknesses are internal; opportunities and threats arise mainly from the external environment.

questions.question: Which factor belongs to a PESTLE analysis?
options: Legal changes affecting organisational communication
The personal preference of one copywriter
The colour of the office furniture
The number of staff birthdays in a month
questions.explanation: PESTLE reviews Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal, and Environmental factors.

questions.question: Which objective is SMART?
options: Improve our image soon
Make everyone like the organisation
Get much more media coverage whenever possible
Increase positive brand sentiment among first-year students by 15% within six months
questions.explanation: A SMART objective is specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound.

questions.question: An objective stating that students should recognise a new university policy is primarily at which level?
options: Attitude
Awareness
Action
Profit
questions.explanation: Awareness objectives concern what the audience should know; attitude concerns feelings, and action concerns behaviour.

questions.question: Why are audience personas useful in PR planning?
options: They clarify audience needs, motivations, and media habits
They guarantee that all stakeholders behave alike
They replace real audience research
They make one message suitable for everyone
questions.explanation: Personas help planners visualise audience segments and tailor messages and channels appropriately.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes strategy from tactics?
options: Strategy is a single social media post, while tactics are long-term goals
Strategy and tactics are identical terms
Strategy is the overall approach, while tactics are the specific actions used to execute it
Tactics define the problem, while strategy only records costs
questions.explanation: A strategy gives direction; tactics include concrete activities such as events, media pitches, videos, or stakeholder meetings.

questions.question: What does the PESO model represent?
options: Public, External, Social, and Organisational media
Paid, Earned, Shared, and Owned media
Planning, Evaluation, Strategy, and Objectives
Promotion, Engagement, Sales, and Outreach
questions.explanation: PESO helps PR planners combine complementary media channels in a balanced communication approach.

questions.question: What do the Barcelona Principles encourage PR practitioners to prioritise?
options: Counting media impressions as the only measure
Using quantitative data and rejecting qualitative evidence
Evaluating a campaign only after all records are lost
Measuring outcomes rather than relying only on outputs
questions.explanation: The Barcelona Principles promote meaningful outcome measurement using both quantitative and qualitative methods.

questions.question: Which PR model seeks publicity and attention with little concern for balanced information?
options: Public information model
Two-way symmetrical model
Press agentry or publicity model
Stakeholder model
questions.explanation: The press agentry model is one-way and publicity-driven, often focusing on attention and persuasion.

questions.question: Which model uses one-way communication to distribute generally factual organisational information?
options: Public information model
Press agentry model
Two-way asymmetrical model
Two-way symmetrical model
questions.explanation: The public information model disseminates factual information but does not primarily seek dialogue or feedback.

questions.question: What characterises the two-way asymmetrical model?
options: Both parties adapt equally through dialogue
Research is used to persuade publics mainly in the organisation's favour
No audience research is conducted
The organisation communicates only through paid advertising
questions.explanation: Two-way asymmetrical PR uses feedback and research, but mainly to make persuasion more effective for the organisation.

questions.question: What characterises the two-way symmetrical model?
options: One-way factual distribution
Manipulative publicity without research
Complete organisational control of stakeholder responses
Dialogue and mutual adjustment between the organisation and its publics
questions.explanation: The symmetrical model aims at mutual understanding, negotiation, and adaptation rather than one-sided persuasion.

questions.question: According to Excellence Theory, where should PR be positioned in an organisation?
options: Within strategic management and decision-making
Outside the organisation as an occasional vendor
Only within the advertising sales unit
At the lowest level with no management access
questions.explanation: Excellence Theory argues that PR contributes most when integrated into management and strategic decisions.

questions.question: A company holds town-hall meetings, listens to community concerns, and changes part of its policy. Which model is illustrated?
options: Press agentry
Public information
Two-way symmetrical communication
One-way propaganda
questions.explanation: The company engages in dialogue and adapts based on stakeholder feedback, which reflects symmetrical communication.

questions.question: What does Systems Theory emphasise in public relations?
options: Organisations can ignore external feedback
Only internal departments influence reputation
Publics have no effect on organisational survival
Organisations are open and interdependent with their environments
questions.explanation: Systems Theory views organisations as interacting with and adapting to stakeholders and environmental forces.

questions.question: Which theory focuses on identifying and managing relationships with groups affected by organisational actions?
options: Cultivation Theory
Stakeholder Theory
Agenda-setting Theory
Social Learning Theory
questions.explanation: Stakeholder Theory directs attention to groups that affect or are affected by organisational decisions.

questions.question: What does agenda-setting theory suggest PR may influence?
options: The private beliefs of every individual with certainty
The legal validity of organisational policies
Which issues audiences consider important
The price of all advertised products
questions.explanation: Agenda setting concerns issue salience: repeated attention can influence what the public sees as important.

questions.question: What is the central concern of cultivation theory?
options: Long-term media exposure can shape perceptions of social reality
Audiences immediately copy every media message
PR campaigns always produce direct sales
Stakeholders only respond to face-to-face communication
questions.explanation: Cultivation theory examines the gradual effect of repeated media representations on audience perceptions.

questions.question: Which traditional PR channel combines sound and, in television, visual presentation for wide reach?
options: Direct mail
Broadcast media
White papers
Internal memoranda
questions.explanation: Radio and television can reach large audiences and use sound or audiovisual presentation for impact.

questions.question: Why do press releases remain useful in the digital era?
options: They guarantee publication by every journalist
They give PR practitioners total control of media coverage
They eliminate the need for contact details
They provide an organised, official source of newsworthy information
questions.explanation: A well-prepared release gives journalists verified facts, quotations, context, and organisational contact information.

questions.question: Which channel is most suitable for a highly detailed technical explanation?
options: A white paper or webinar
A five-second audio tag
A single-word social post
A brief event invitation
questions.explanation: Complex messages need formats that allow explanation, evidence, and audience questions.

questions.question: What is a major advantage of social media as a PR channel?
options: Complete protection from criticism
Automatic accuracy of all user content
Direct, real-time engagement with publics
Guaranteed access to every demographic
questions.explanation: Social platforms enable rapid dialogue, community building, feedback, and direct distribution without relying solely on traditional gatekeepers.

questions.question: What is earned media?
options: Content published on an organisation's own website
Advertising space purchased by the organisation
Private messages sent to employees
Unpaid coverage or discussion gained through newsworthiness and relationships
questions.explanation: Earned media includes organic news coverage, reviews, mentions, and discussions generated without buying the placement.

questions.question: Why must cultural context influence channel selection?
options: Culture determines that only one channel may be used
Communication habits and interpretations differ across communities
Every region interprets all symbols identically
Cultural analysis is relevant only to advertising
questions.explanation: Cultural sensitivity helps practitioners choose accessible channels and avoid messages that may be misunderstood or offensive.

questions.question: What is the primary focus of lobbying?
options: Selling products directly to consumers
Producing entertainment for the general public
Influencing specific legislation, regulations, or policy decisions
Managing only employee newsletters
questions.explanation: Lobbying usually involves direct engagement with policymakers concerning specific policies or legislation.

questions.question: How is advocacy generally broader than lobbying?
options: It may influence public opinion as well as policy through campaigns and mobilisation
It is limited to private meetings with legislators
It excludes media engagement
It cannot address social causes
questions.explanation: Advocacy can include awareness campaigns, grassroots action, media engagement, education, and policy proposals.

questions.question: Which activity is most clearly a lobbying tactic?
options: Organising a public awareness concert
Presenting a policy brief directly to legislators
Publishing a community storytelling video
Holding an employee social event
questions.explanation: Direct interaction with lawmakers to influence a specific policy is a typical lobbying activity.

questions.question: Which ethical concern can arise when lobbyists have unequal access to decision-makers?
options: All policy decisions automatically become transparent
Public participation always increases equally
Misinformation becomes impossible
Some interests may gain disproportionate influence
questions.explanation: Unequal access can distort representation, create undue influence, and reduce trust in policymaking.

questions.question: Why should a PR practitioner research a journalist's beat before pitching?
options: To align the story with the journalist's area of interest
To avoid including any news value
To send an identical pitch to every reporter
To determine the price of advertising space
questions.explanation: A tailored pitch is more relevant and more likely to receive attention than a mass, unrelated message.

questions.question: What behaviour most helps a PR professional become a trusted media source?
options: Sending repeated messages after a journalist declines
Withholding key facts until publication
Providing accurate information promptly and consistently
Offering only exaggerated promotional claims
questions.explanation: Reliability, accuracy, responsiveness, and honesty build long-term trust with journalists.

questions.question: Which structure places the most important facts first in a press release?
options: Chronological suspense structure
Problem-solution essay structure
Circular narrative structure
The inverted pyramid
questions.explanation: The inverted pyramid begins with the key facts, followed by supporting details in decreasing order of importance.

questions.question: What is normally included in the boilerplate of a press release?
options: A confidential list of journalists
A brief standard description of the organisation
The journalist's final headline
The full campaign budget
questions.explanation: The boilerplate gives reusable background information about the organisation near the end of the release.

questions.question: How does a media kit differ from a press release?
options: A media kit contains less information than a headline
A press release is always paid advertising
A media kit contains several supporting resources, while a press release presents one main announcement
A media kit is used only for internal employees
questions.explanation: Media kits may contain fact sheets, biographies, photographs, background documents, releases, and contact information.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of media training for a spokesperson?
options: To deliver key messages clearly and handle difficult questions confidently
To avoid every interview request
To memorise false answers
To control the journalist's final report
questions.explanation: Training prepares spokespersons to remain accurate, concise, composed, and consistent under questioning.

questions.question: Which preparation is most important before a press conference?
options: Invite journalists without deciding what will be announced
Define objectives, prepare materials, select spokespersons, and anticipate questions
Allow every employee to give a different message
Avoid checking the venue or technology
questions.explanation: Detailed preparation improves message clarity, logistics, spokesperson performance, and media usefulness.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a professional code of ethics in PR?
options: To guarantee that practitioners never face dilemmas
To replace all national laws
To promote organisational interests at any cost
To guide responsible conduct and protect public trust
questions.explanation: Codes set standards such as honesty, fairness, accuracy, confidentiality, and responsibility.

questions.question: A practitioner discovers that a client intends to publish fabricated survey results. What is the most ethical response?
options: Refuse to distribute the false claim and advise correction
Publish it because the client is paying
Remove the sample size but retain the false result
Present the fabrication as an anonymous source
questions.explanation: Professional integrity requires refusing deceptive communication and encouraging accurate disclosure.

questions.question: When may confidentiality be ethically limited?
options: Whenever a competitor requests information
Whenever a journalist wants a faster story
When keeping information secret would conceal serious unlawful or harmful conduct
Whenever disclosure could attract publicity
questions.explanation: Confidentiality is important, but it does not justify assisting illegality or concealing serious threats to the public.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of employee communication?
options: To prevent employees from giving feedback
To communicate only during disciplinary action
To replace all operational management
To create understanding and alignment between the organisation and employees
questions.explanation: Effective internal communication helps employees understand goals, roles, decisions, and expectations.

questions.question: How can clear internal communication improve productivity?
options: Employees receive more conflicting instructions
Employees better understand priorities, responsibilities, and procedures
Managers no longer need to set objectives
All workplace disagreements disappear automatically
questions.explanation: Clarity reduces uncertainty, duplication, errors, and wasted effort.

questions.question: Why is two-way internal communication important for engagement?
options: Employees feel heard and can contribute useful feedback
It prevents leaders from sharing information
It ensures every employee agrees with management
It removes the need for formal channels
questions.explanation: Dialogue increases trust, participation, and the sense that employees are valued.

questions.question: During organisational change, what should internal PR prioritise?
options: Rumours and informal leaks
Silence until every detail is final
Timely explanations, empathy, feedback channels, and consistent updates
Different instructions from each department
questions.explanation: Transparent communication manages expectations and reduces fear, confusion, and resistance during change.

questions.question: Why should internal messages be segmented?
options: Segmentation allows leaders to conceal all shared goals
Different roles and departments may need different levels of detail
Every employee uses the same technical language
It removes the need for organisational consistency
questions.explanation: Segmentation improves relevance while core facts and organisational values remain consistent.

questions.question: What is the value of a multi-channel internal communication approach?
options: It guarantees every channel carries a different message
It eliminates the need to evaluate communication
It restricts information to office-based employees
It reaches employees through formats suited to different needs and work contexts
questions.explanation: Email, meetings, intranets, video, mobile alerts, and printed materials can complement one another across a diverse workforce.

questions.question: How can storytelling support internal PR?
options: It replaces factual information with fiction
It prevents employees from asking questions
It makes organisational values and goals memorable through relatable examples
It is useful only for external advertising
questions.explanation: Stories can illustrate values, recognise employee contributions, and connect strategy to real experience.

questions.question: What is a major benefit of visual communication inside an organisation?
options: It can simplify complex information and improve recall
It guarantees that written explanations are never required
It is understood identically across all cultures
It removes accessibility concerns
questions.explanation: Infographics, diagrams, and videos can improve comprehension when designed clearly and accessibly.

questions.question: Why should internal and external PR messages be coordinated?
options: Internal messages should always contradict public statements
Employees should learn major decisions from rumours
External PR has no effect on employees
Employees and external publics should receive a coherent organisational narrative
questions.explanation: Alignment reduces confusion and enables informed employees to act as credible brand ambassadors.

questions.question: Which method best evaluates an internal communication programme?
options: Count only the number of emails sent
Use surveys, feedback, engagement data, and evidence of understanding
Assume silence means full understanding
Evaluate only the design of the newsletter
questions.explanation: Evaluation should assess whether messages were received, understood, trusted, and acted upon, not merely distributed.

questions.question: What makes PR in a non-profit organisation distinctive?
options: Non-profits have no stakeholders
Non-profit PR focuses only on product sales
Communication is strongly centred on mission, social impact, donors, and community support
Non-profits do not need reputation management
questions.explanation: Non-profit PR must explain the mission, demonstrate impact, attract support, and maintain trust despite limited resources.

questions.question: Why is transparency especially important to donors?
options: They want evidence that funds are used responsibly and produce impact
It allows the organisation to avoid reporting outcomes
It guarantees donations without engagement
It removes the need for financial controls
questions.explanation: Regular, honest reporting on income, spending, activities, and outcomes strengthens donor confidence.

questions.question: Why is storytelling powerful in non-profit PR?
options: It allows facts and consent to be ignored
It connects the mission to human experiences that audiences can understand emotionally
It guarantees that every story becomes viral
It replaces accountability reports
questions.explanation: Ethical stories make social problems and programme outcomes relatable while supporting the organisation's case for action.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of diversified fundraising channels?
options: They eliminate the need for donor relationships
They make accountability unnecessary
They prevent community participation
They reduce dependence on a single source of income
questions.explanation: Using grants, individual donations, events, partnerships, and digital appeals can reduce financial risk.

questions.question: What is the primary goal of building community support for a non-profit?
options: Fostering shared ownership, participation, and collaboration
Keeping all decisions within the organisation
Replacing local leaders with external consultants
Obtaining publicity without community involvement
questions.explanation: Community support is strongest when people see the mission as relevant, participate in decisions, and contribute to solutions.

questions.question: How can local leaders strengthen a non-profit's community relations?
options: They guarantee that no disagreement will occur
They eliminate the need for stakeholder analysis
They provide credibility, networks, and knowledge of community needs
They should communicate only with donors outside the community
questions.explanation: Trusted teachers, business owners, traditional leaders, and other community figures can improve access and legitimacy.

questions.question: What is the central purpose of public-sector PR?
options: To maximise private profit from government information
To prevent public scrutiny
To replace policymaking with publicity
To manage communication between government institutions and citizens in support of public service
questions.explanation: Public-sector PR informs citizens, supports transparency, builds trust, encourages participation, and manages crises.

questions.question: Which challenge is particularly common in public-sector PR?
options: The absence of any legal duties
Complex bureaucracy and political influence
Freedom from public scrutiny
No need to communicate during emergencies
questions.explanation: Government communication often operates within administrative procedures, political pressures, legal requirements, and intense public scrutiny.

questions.question: Which strategy best promotes trust in government communication?
options: Delay updates until rumours dominate
Use technical jargon to discourage questions
Provide clear, accurate information and create opportunities for public dialogue
Release different facts through different agencies
questions.explanation: Transparency, consistency, responsiveness, and engagement support credibility in public institutions.

questions.question: How can grassroots mobilisation support advocacy?
options: It demonstrates broad public support and encourages participation in policy change
It limits communication to private legislative meetings
It prevents media attention
It replaces research with unverified claims
questions.explanation: Grassroots mobilisation engages citizens through petitions, meetings, events, and coordinated action, showing policymakers the depth of support.

questions.question: What is a KPI in public relations?
options: A general slogan with no target
A specific measurable indicator used to assess PR performance
A list of journalists invited to an event
A legal rule governing all communication
questions.explanation: Key Performance Indicators translate PR objectives into measurable signs of progress or success.

questions.question: Which metric is an output rather than an outcome?
options: A measurable increase in stakeholder trust
A change in public behaviour
Improved employee retention linked to communication
The number of press releases distributed
questions.explanation: Outputs record what PR produced; outcomes measure changes in awareness, attitudes, behaviour, or organisational performance.

questions.question: What does quantitative media analysis examine?
options: Only the emotional meaning of quotations
The personal intentions of every journalist
Measurable features such as volume, reach, prominence, and frequency of coverage
The organisation's internal payroll
questions.explanation: Quantitative analysis counts observable media indicators, while qualitative analysis examines tone, framing, message accuracy, and sentiment.

questions.question: What can stakeholder surveys measure in PR evaluation?
options: Awareness, attitudes, perceptions, and reported behaviour
Only the number of media releases issued
The exact future actions of every respondent
Advertising prices across all outlets
questions.explanation: Surveys gather structured evidence about what stakeholders know, feel, believe, and say they have done.

questions.question: Which web-analytics result most directly indicates that a PR call to action produced behaviour?
options: The total number of pages on the website
The age of the website domain
The number of staff who drafted the message
The conversion rate for the intended action
questions.explanation: A conversion measures completion of a desired action such as registration, donation, download, or enquiry.

questions.question: What is benchmarking in PR evaluation?
options: Replacing campaign objectives after completion
Comparing performance with past results, competitors, or industry standards
Counting only positive comments
Avoiding comparisons to protect reputation
questions.explanation: Benchmarking provides a reference point for identifying strengths, gaps, and realistic improvement targets.

questions.question: Why must KPIs align with organisational objectives?
options: Metrics should show whether PR contributes to outcomes the organisation values
Every available metric should be reported regardless of relevance
Alignment makes evaluation unnecessary
PR should measure only media coverage
questions.explanation: Relevant KPIs connect communication activity to strategic goals instead of producing disconnected statistics.

questions.question: What should a comprehensive PR report include?
options: Only screenshots of positive coverage
A list of activities without analysis
Objectives, KPIs, results, interpretation, and recommendations
Raw data with no explanation or conclusion
questions.explanation: A useful report explains what was intended, what happened, why it matters, and what should be improved.

questions.question: How does storytelling improve a PR evaluation presentation?
options: It allows unfavourable results to be hidden
It connects data to a clear narrative about the campaign's purpose and impact
It replaces evidence with emotional claims
It makes visual aids unnecessary
